## What Alloq is

Alloq is a web app that helps a software team plan which people work on which project in each week. It counts the free capacity of each person after absences, public holidays, part time and internal work. It also shows the state of all projects on one page. Alloq runs in the browser, and there is also a macOS desktop app that works on the same central database.

## Who uses Alloq

Alloq has four personas:

- **Administrator.** An administrator decides who can sign in and what each person may read or change. The administrator also keeps the roles, daily rates, departments and public holidays.
- **Project manager.** A project manager plans people on projects week by week and keeps the data, status and risks of each project current.
- **Employee.** An employee reads the planning and the projects without changing them and keeps their own account up to date.
- **Desktop user.** A desktop user works in the macOS app and signs in with a Microsoft account.

The [story map](/features/story-map) describes the goals of each persona in more detail.

## How the docs are organised

The docs follow the Diátaxis model, which sorts pages by what the reader wants to do. There are four sections:

- **Guide.** These pages show you how to set up Alloq and how to contribute a change.
- **Architecture.** These pages explain how Alloq is built and why.
- **Features.** The story map lists all user stories by activity. Each feature page holds the stories of one part of the app.
- **Reference.** These pages list the commands, the configuration, the test setup and the glossary, so you can look up a single fact.

## How the stories link to the code

# Getting started

This page takes you from a fresh clone to a running Alloq web app on your machine.
At the end you can sign in, change code and run the same checks as the CI.

## What you need

- **Python 3.14.** You do not have to install it yourself. `task init` reads
  `requires-python = ">=3.14"` from [pyproject.toml](../../pyproject.toml) and
  installs that version with uv.
- **uv**, the package manager. The repo is a uv workspace with the host app and
  four packages under `components/`.
- **Task**, the task runner. Every command on this page is a `task` target. See
  [Commands](../reference/commands.md) for the full list.
- **PostgreSQL 15 or newer.** You can use your own server or the `db` service in
  [docker-compose.yml](../../docker-compose.yml).
- **ty**, the type checker, for `task typecheck`. It is not a dependency in
  `pyproject.toml`, so install it yourself and make sure it is on your `PATH`.
- **Node.js**, only if you build these docs or run the JavaScript tests.
- **Rust and the Xcode command line tools**, only if you work on the desktop app.
  The comments in [taskfiles/Taskfile.reflex.yml](../../taskfiles/Taskfile.reflex.yml)
  list them.

## 1. Create the `.env` file

The app reads its settings from YAML files in `configuration/` and from
environment variables. A `.env` file in the repo root is loaded on start, so put
your local values there. Start from [.env.example](../../.env.example) and copy it
to `.env`. Git ignores `.env`.

Set these three lines first:

```bash
PROFILES=local
SECRET_PROVIDER=local
UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv.mac
```

- `PROFILES=local` loads `configuration/config.local.yaml` on top of
  `configuration/config.yaml`.
- `SECRET_PROVIDER=local` makes the app read secrets from environment variables
  instead of Azure Key Vault.
- `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv.mac` is the virtual environment the team uses on
  macOS. Any other folder name works too.

### Secrets

[configuration/config.yaml](../../configuration/config.yaml) refers to secrets with
values such as `secret:alloq-db-user`. With the local provider, the app looks for
an environment variable with that name. It tries the name as written, in upper
case, and with dashes turned into underscores (`ALLOQ_DB_USER`). The lookup is
`_get_secret_from_env` in appkit_commons.

The `local` profile needs these secrets:

| Secret in `config.yaml` | Environment variable | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `alloq-db-user` | `ALLOQ_DB_USER` | Postgres user |
| `alloq-db-password` | `ALLOQ_DB_PASSWORD` | Postgres password |
| `alloq-db-host` | `ALLOQ_DB_HOST` | Postgres host |
| `alloq-db-name` | `ALLOQ_DB_NAME` | Postgres database name |
| `common-db-encryption-key` | `COMMON_DB_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | Fernet key that appkit uses to encrypt stored OAuth tokens |
| `common-oauth-azure-client-id` | `COMMON_OAUTH_AZURE_CLIENT_ID` | Client id of the Microsoft sign-in |
| `common-oauth-azure-client-secret` | `COMMON_OAUTH_AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` | Client secret of the Microsoft sign-in |
| `common-oauth-azure-tenant-id` | `COMMON_OAUTH_AZURE_TENANT_ID` | Entra tenant id |

The Azure values are needed because `config.local.yaml` keeps the Azure provider
from `config.yaml`. If you do not use Microsoft sign-in locally, any text works,
and the CI workflow in [.github/workflows/ci.yml](../../.github/workflows/ci.yml)
sets them to `ci`. You can create a Fernet key with the same command the CI uses:

```bash
uv run python -c 'from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())'
```

::: warning Names in .env.example
`.env.example` still uses older secret names (`mn-db-user`, `avui-db-encryption-key`).
They do not match the `secret:` references in `config.yaml`. Use the names in the
table above.
:::

Never commit real credentials. Production reads the same names from Azure Key
Vault. See [Configuration](../reference/configuration.md) for how profiles, secrets
and environment overrides work together.

## 2. Start a database

If you use the Compose database, start only the `db` service:

```bash
docker compose up -d db
```

It creates the database `alloq-db` with user and password `REDACTED` and publishes
it on host port `5433`. `config.yaml` uses port `5432`, so override the port in
`.env`:

```bash
ALLOQ_DB_HOST=localhost
ALLOQ_DB_NAME=alloq-db
ALLOQ_DB_USER=REDACTED
ALLOQ_DB_PASSWORD=REDACTED
APP__DATABASE__PORT=5433
```

`APP__DATABASE__PORT` uses the double underscore override that
[Configuration](../reference/configuration.md#environment-overrides) explains.

## 3. Initialize the project

```bash
task init
```

`task init` runs these steps from [Taskfile.dist.yml](../../Taskfile.dist.yml):

1. It installs and pins the Python version from `pyproject.toml`.
2. It runs `uv sync`. This installs the dev and desktop dependency groups, because
   `pyproject.toml` sets them as default groups.
3. It installs pre-commit if it is missing and runs `pre-commit install`.
4. It runs `alembic upgrade head`, so the database must be reachable at this point.

Later, when dependencies change, `task sync` is enough. To apply new migrations, run
`task db:upgrade`.

## 4. Run the app

```bash
task run
```

`task run` calls `reflex run`. With the `local` profile, the app is served at
`http://localhost:8080/alloq`. The port and the `/alloq` path prefix come from
`frontend_port` and `frontend_path` in
[configuration/config.local.yaml](../../configuration/config.local.yaml). The
backend listens on port `3030` from `config.yaml`.

- `task run:debug` starts the same app with debug logging.
- `task run:prod` starts it in Reflex production mode on one port.

When `app.environment` is `production`, the app refuses to start without the
`PUBLIC_BASE_URL` environment variable (`configure()` in
[app/configuration.py](../../app/configuration.py)). The base profile and the `prod`
profile set `production`. The `local` profile sets `local`, so you do not need the
variable on your machine.

The planning page ("Ressourcenplanung" [resource planning]) opens at `/` and at
`/plan`. All other pages are in the sidebar.

## 5. Sign in

The login page ("Anmelden" [sign in]) has an email and password form and a
"Mit Microsoft anmelden" [sign in with Microsoft] button.

The baseline migration seeds one administrator account with the email `admin`.
A later migration flags it with `needs_password_reset`, so the app asks for a new
password. Ask a team member for the local test login. Use it only against your
local database, and never commit it or write it into a file in the repo.

What a signed-in user can see and do depends on the role. Administrators can do
everything. Project managers edit planning. Employees only read. See
[Security and access](../architecture/security-and-access.md).

::: tip "reading 'length'" after a code change
If the browser shows this error after you added a state class, reload the page and
sign in again. The browser still holds the old state shape. It is not a bug in
your code.
:::

## 6. Run the quality gates

Run these before you push. On every pull request and every push to `main`, the CI
runs `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `pytest` and the JavaScript tests. It
does not run the type check or the coverage limit, so run those yourself.

```bash
task format     # ruff check --fix, then ruff format
task lint       # ruff check .
task typecheck  # ty check app
task test       # pytest --cov, fails below 80 % coverage
```

### Setup in Azure, done once

App registration. The values are in `app.desktop` of `config.desktop.yaml`. They
point to the entries of the web app with `secret:`. At build time,
`scripts/desktop.py` resolves them and writes the plain values into the app. This
is only allowed for the public identifiers in `BUILD_TIME_KEYS`: `tenant_id`,
`client_id`, `host` and `name`. Any other `secret:` stops the build with a
`BuildError`. The registration needs these settings:

- The platform "Mobile and desktop applications" with the redirect URI
  `http://localhost`.
- "Allow public client flows" set to yes. The desktop app sends no client secret.
- The delegated API permission "Azure OSSRDBMS Database" with
  `user_impersonation`, with admin consent. The scope in the code is
  `https://ossrdbms-aad.database.windows.net/.default` (`POSTGRES_SCOPE`).

# Alloq **Resource management & capacity planning for software teams** ![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-2.0.4-blue) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](LICENSE.md) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.14%2B-orange)](https://www.python.org) [![Reflex](https://img.shields.io/badge/reflex-0.10.0-purple)](https://reflex.dev) [Features](#features) • [Documentation](#documentation) • [Getting Started](#getting-started) • [Development](#development) • [Deployment](#deployment)
--- Alloq helps software teams plan which people work on which project in each week. It counts the free capacity of each person after absences, public holidays, part time and internal work, and it shows the state of all projects on one page. Alloq runs in the browser, and there is also a macOS desktop app that works on the same central database. ## Features - **Resource Planning** — Weekly capacity grid that you edit like a spreadsheet, with filters and an absence timeline - **Staffing** — Staff a project with the "Projekt planen" wizard or person by person in the project drawer - **Projects** — Project cards and an inspector with status, period, status reports, earned value chart and risks - **Portfolio Overview** — Health of all projects at a glance, with time and progress, risk grid and staffing capacity - **Team** — Employees, roles, seniority levels, departments and absences - **Master Data** — Roles, departments, region-aware public holidays and daily rates with margin-based pricing - **Authentication** — Email and password sign-in and Microsoft sign-in (Entra ID) - **Role-Based Access** — Administrators can do everything, project managers edit planning, employees only read - **Desktop App** — macOS app (Tauri) that signs in with Entra ID and connects to Postgres with a personal token ## Documentation The developer documentation starts at [docs/index.md](docs/index.md). It covers setup, architecture, the user stories of each feature, and reference pages, and it describes v2.0.4. ```bash # Install the docs dependencies once task docs:install # Start the docs site with live reload task docs:dev ``` ## Tech Stack | Layer | Technology | | ----- | ---------- | | Framework | [Reflex](https://reflex.dev) 0.10.0 (full-stack Python) | | UI Components | [appkit_mantine](https://github.com/jenreh/appkit) (Mantine 9.5) | | Database | PostgreSQL 15 + SQLModel/SQLAlchemy 2.0 | | Migrations | Alembic (manually authored) | | Auth | appkit-user (session-based + OAuth) | | Desktop | Tauri + reflex-desktop | | Docs | VitePress | | Task Runner | [Task](https://taskfile.dev) | | Package Manager | [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) | ## Getting Started The full walkthrough is in [Getting started](docs/guide/getting-started.md). The short version follows. ### Prerequisites - [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager (`task init` installs Python 3.14 with it) - [Task](https://taskfile.dev) runner - PostgreSQL 15+ (or the `db` service in Docker Compose) - [ty](https://github.com/astral-sh/ty) on your `PATH` for `task typecheck` - Node.js, only for the docs and the JavaScript tests ### Configuration Settings come from the YAML files in `configuration/` and from environment variables. Put your local values in a `.env` file in the repo root: ```bash PROFILES=local SECRET_PROVIDER=local UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv.mac ``` `PROFILES=local` loads `configuration/config.local.yaml` on top of `configuration/config.yaml`. With `SECRET_PROVIDER=local`, the `secret:` values in the config are read from environment variables, for example `ALLOQ_DB_USER` for `secret:alloq-db-user`. The [Getting started](docs/guide/getting-started.md#secrets) guide lists every secret the local profile needs. To use the Compose database, start only that service. It listens on host port `5433`: ```bash docker compose up -d db ``` ### Installation ```bash # Clone the repository git clone https://github.com/jenreh/alloq.git cd alloq # Initialize project (installs Python, syncs deps, sets up pre-commit, runs migrations) task init ``` `task init` runs the migrations, so the database must be reachable at this point. ### Running ```bash # Start the development server task run # Or with debug logging task run:debug ``` With the `local` profile, the app is available at `http://localhost:8080/alloq`. ## Development ### Project Structure ```text app/ # Host Reflex app (pages, admin pages, desktop sign-in, styles) components/ alloq-commons/ # Shared entities, repositories, models, services, excel_grid alloq-dashboard/ # Portfolio overview (aggregation, charts) alloq-project/ # Project planning & forecasting alloq-team/ # Team management views configuration/ # YAML config files (per-environment profiles) alembic/ # Database migrations docs/ # Developer documentation (VitePress) tauri/ # macOS desktop app shell scripts/ # Desktop build and helper scripts tests/ # Integration tests ``` Each `components/*` package is a uv workspace member with its own `pyproject.toml` and test suite. ### Common Tasks ```bash task run # Start the app with hot reload task test # Run tests with coverage task test:js # Run JavaScript unit tests (node --test) task lint # Lint with ruff task format # Auto-format with ruff task typecheck # Type check app/ with ty task db:upgrade # Apply pending migrations task db:revision -- "description" # Create new migration task desktop:dev # Run the desktop app against the local database ``` [Commands](docs/reference/commands.md) lists every target. ### Quality Gates - Test coverage ≥ 80% for non-Reflex classes and State classes - `ruff` linting and formatting (line length 88) - `ty` type checks - Pre-commit hooks for secrets detection and formatting ## Screenshots ### Resource Planning Weekly capacity grid with per-employee allocation, over/under-utilization highlighting, and role badges. Each employee's planned projects are sorted alphabetically by display name, ignoring case. The calendar button beside each employee's “+” opens absence entry. Saving updates the planning grid and keeps unsaved allocation edits. The **Abwesenheiten** tab next to **Projekte** shows Gantt bars for employees with absences overlapping the selected time range. It shares the planning filters, with exact dates on hover. ![Resource Planning](docs/images/planning.png) Capacities are edited like in a spreadsheet (reusable `excel_grid` component in `alloq_commons.components.excel_grid`). Selection, navigation and editing run in the browser; only committed values are sent to the server, and changes are kept until you save — also when switching the time range (edits outside the new range stay pending and are saved too). Leaving the page with unsaved changes (sidebar, links, Back) asks whether to stay, discard or save & leave; closing or reloading the tab shows the browser's warning. | Keys | Action | | --- | --- | | Arrow keys | Move; ↓/↑ continue into the next/previous employee (or project) | | Ctrl+Arrow | Jump to the edge of the current employee block, then to the next one | | Home / End, Ctrl+Home / Ctrl+End, PageUp / PageDown | Row start/end, first/last cell, page | | Tab / Shift+Tab, Enter / Shift+Enter | Move right/left, down/up (also commits an edit) | | Type a number, F2, double-click | Edit (typing replaces, F2 keeps the value); Esc cancels | | Shift+Arrow, Shift+click, mouse drag, Ctrl+A | Select a range (Ctrl+A: employee block, twice: all) | | Ctrl+C / Ctrl+X / Ctrl+V | Copy/cut/paste as tab-separated values (works with Excel) | | Delete / Backspace | Clear selection | | Ctrl+D / Ctrl+R | Fill down / right | | Drag the fill handle (small square at the selection's bottom-right) | Copy the selected value(s) into the dragged-over cells; Esc cancels | | Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y | Undo / redo | | Ctrl+S | Save | ### Projects Project cards with budget, progress, team members, and risk indicators. ![Projects](docs/images/projects.png) ### Team Overview Employee cards with roles, seniority levels, and absence periods. ![Team Overview](docs/images/people.png) ### Administration User management with activation, verification, and role assignment. ![Administration](docs/images/admin.png) ## Deployment For desktop access with Entra ID, follow the [Azure setup](docs/architecture/desktop.md#setup-in-azure-done-once) in the desktop architecture page. After migrating, grant `alloq_app` with `ADMIN OPTION` to the actual Entra admin principal; Azure's protected `azure_pg_admin` role must remain unchanged. ### Docker ```bash # Build and start with Docker Compose (includes PostgreSQL) docker compose up --build ``` The Compose setup includes: - Application container (Python 3.14 slim) - PostgreSQL 15 with pgvector - Dev-mode file watching with `docker compose watch` ### Environment Variables Production secrets are referenced via `secret:` prefix in config and resolved from environment variables or a Key Vault at runtime. See `configuration/config.yaml` for the full list and [Configuration](docs/reference/configuration.md) for how profiles, secrets and overrides work together. > [!NOTE] > Never commit credentials. Use `.env` files locally and proper secret management in production. ### Serving below a path prefix The app can run below a URL prefix (for example `/alloq`) behind a reverse proxy that serves the exported frontend and passes every other path under the prefix to the backend (mount mode, appkit 1.16). The public address comes from two variables, read by `app/public_url.py`: | Variable | Export | Backend | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://apps.example.com` | yes | yes | Origin of the site. Production refuses to start without it. The auth server URL, the OAuth callback URLs and the Reflex URLs are derived from it. | | `PUBLIC_PATH_PREFIX=/alloq` | yes | yes | The prefix. Callbacks become `/alloq/oauth//callback`, with no port. | | `REFLEX_FRONTEND_PATH=/alloq` | yes | yes | Prefixes assets and the router basename, and names the session cookie (`alloq_session`). Also set by `frontend_path` in the config. | | `REFLEX_BACKEND_PATH=/alloq` | yes | yes | Mounts the backend routes under the prefix. | | `REFLEX_API_URL=http://localhost:8080` | yes | yes | The origin of the websocket. A `localhost` host is swapped for the page's host in the browser. | ```bash export PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080 PUBLIC_PATH_PREFIX=/alloq \ REFLEX_FRONTEND_PATH=/alloq REFLEX_BACKEND_PATH=/alloq \ REFLEX_API_URL=http://localhost:8080 reflex export --frontend-only --no-zip # output: .web/build/client/alloq reflex run --env prod --backend-only --backend-port 8002 ``` Use `/alloq/ping` as the health probe. Reflex's `/_health` needs `reflex[db]`, which this app does not install.
